title: A letter from Nairobi
text:
14 Jacaranda Close
Nairobi, Kenya
3 November

Dear Dewi,

Thank you for your letter and the photograph of batik day at your school. I laughed out loud when I saw your teacher's shirt. It was the brightest orange I have ever seen!

You asked what the rainy season is like here. In Nairobi the long rains come between March and May, and the short rains arrive in November, which is now. Most mornings are sunny, and the clouds gather after lunch. By four o'clock the sky is dark grey and the rain drums on our tin roof so loudly that Mum and I have to shout to hear each other.

Last week, the rain gave us a small adventure. The road outside school filled with water, so the bus could not get through. Mr Otieno, our teacher, said we would wait in the library until the water went down. We read comics and played chess until six o'clock, when my father arrived in his big boots. He carried my little brother across the flooded road on his shoulders, and I walked behind, trying not to laugh.

I have a favourite thing about the rain, though. The morning after a storm the air smells fresh and clean, and the garden is full of weaver birds. They hang upside down from the thin branches and mend their nests, chattering all the time as if they are arguing about the best way to do it.

You told me that your school has a vegetable garden. Ours does too. We grow sukuma wiki, a leafy green vegetable that Mum cooks with onions and tomatoes. Do you grow anything that you can eat? Please tell me how you cook it.

Please write soon and tell me about Bandung. I found it on the map, and it looks as if it is surrounded by mountains. Is it cool there?

Your friend,
Amara
